why: Applying the independence rule to the estate's real history returns the same answer for all five closed chains: no independent acceptor has re-examined any of these fixes. chains.title: git push printed Everything up-to-date and exited 0 while publishing nothing

nodes.title: A detached HEAD committed, the branch ref never moved, and push exited 0
nodes.statement: Lane B built a bare remote and a working clone, published a branch, detached HEAD as a shared worktree does, committed, then pushed the branch. git printed 'Everything up-to-date' and exited 0. The remote continued to serve the pre-push commit; the new commit was never published.
nodes.provenance_basis: The silent-push no-op that made a lane's reported head unpublishable. Reproduced end to end by lane B in this run rather than quoted.

nodes.title: DEF-ZERO-EXIT-IS-NOT-PUBLICATION
nodes.statement: A zero exit code from git push is not evidence of publication. A lane can report a commit it never published, and every downstream check that trusts the report inherits a head that does not exist on the remote.

evidence_citations.quote: A lane sharing a detached HEAD can commit, then `git push` a branch ref that never moved. Git prints "Everything up-to-date" and exits 0, so a zero exit is not evidence of publication. Only the remote ref is evidence.

nodes.title: lane_guard.verify_reported_head
nodes.statement: The reported SHA is compared against git ls-remote. A branch the remote does not hold yields REPORTED_BUT_ABSENT; a mismatch yields SILENT_PUSH_DIVERGENCE. Only the remote ref is evidence.
nodes.non_chronological_reason: The mechanism was written on 2026-08-23 from an earlier live occurrence of this defect. Lane B's reproduction on 2026-08-27 is a fresh direct reproduction of the same defect against a disposable remote, recorded because the lane needed the defect in hand rather than quoted. The mechanism therefore predates this chain's observation node; the observation is not the first occurrence and does not claim to be.

chains.title: A hash-valid truncated JSON artifact passed manifest closure

nodes.title: Closure passed on a file that cannot be loaded
nodes.statement: Lane B wrote a truncated JSON artifact, hashed its bytes, entered it in a manifest with a correct bundle digest, and ran verify_manifest_closure. Closure passed. verify_artifact_validity refused the same artifact for not parsing. Byte integrity says the bytes are the committed bytes and says nothing about whether they mean anything.
nodes.provenance_basis: The live occurrence recorded in verify_artifact_validity: a lane published a truncated JSON file whose digest matched its manifest exactly and whose closure check passed. Reproduced by lane B against the live modules.

evidence_citations.quote: Found live: a lane published a truncated JSON file whose digest matched its manifest exactly and whose closure check passed.

nodes.title: DEF-BYTE-INTEGRITY-IS-NOT-SEMANTIC-VALIDITY
nodes.statement: Manifest closure and hash binding are transport controls. A structured artifact nobody can load is not evidence, and no digest can rescue it, because the digest is of the broken bytes.

nodes.title: evidence_integrity.verify_artifact_validity
nodes.statement: Every hash-bound .json artifact is parsed after read-back. A file that does not load, or does not decode as UTF-8, is an error regardless of its digest.
nodes.non_chronological_reason: The mechanism was written on 2026-08-23 from the original live occurrence. Lane B's observation node is a fresh reproduction dated 2026-08-27 and does not claim to be the first occurrence; the original is cited alongside it.

The last two matter as much as the first: a validity check that reports on files it was never given is a different defect.

nodes.statement: The project root is /workspace, whose .cursor directory contains only environment.json: hooks.json is not there at all. git rebase --abort and gh workflow list, both matched by the hooks.json 'git|gh ' matcher, executed through the agent shell tool. The single write-scope audit log on the filesystem stayed at 3 lines and no audit file was created in the lane worktree.

nodes.title: DEF-WRITE-SCOPE-GUARD-UNREACHED-FROM-WORKTREE
nodes.statement: Every boundary in .cursor/write-scope.json is documentation in this runtime. require_write_declaration: true cannot auto-refuse anything, because the hook that would refuse is never reached. write_admission.py still refuses correctly when invoked by hand, so enforcement is voluntary and lane-side, and a lane that skips it is stopped by nothing.
nodes.provenance_basis: DEF-WRITE-SCOPE-GUARD-UNREACHED-FROM-WORKTREE. This is the third time this estate has hit the same class: a rule written in prose and enforced by nothing.

pending_successor.reason: The fix belongs to whoever owns the binding between the Cursor project root and the lane worktrees, not to a lane writing inside one worktree. Lane B will not close this chain on a mechanism it did not ship, and will not invent one to make the chain look finished.
candidate_mechanisms: Carry .cursor/hooks.json and .cursor/hooks/** onto the ref the project root checks out, so the only path Cursor consults is populated.
Install a per-worktree git pre-push hook calling write_admission.py, which fires where the write happens and does not depend on the provider reading a project root.
Make lane_guard.py refuse at integration any lane branch with no admitted write declaration recorded for its head, keeping enforcement lane-side but non-optional.

nodes.title: An integrity ERROR fired on an artifact nobody tampered with
nodes.statement: currentctl compile emits EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH at ERROR severity on urn:obzio:l4:workstream:WS-SO02-CONTROL-PLANE, because the ledger's recorded digest for scctl.py no longer matches the working tree. Walking this branch's history for that path shows the recorded digest e6d0b2d8 was correct at commit 9887f33e, was moved to 76b2ca1f by the authorised EC-13 purge at 3b97d6ff, and was moved again to 70a6494a by this lane's own admitted write at a1592234. Two authorised changes, two identical integrity alarms, no tampering at any point.
nodes.provenance_basis: DEF-SCP-01, found by the coordinator during verification of lane E and reproduced independently here. The coordinator's hash walk ended at 76b2ca1f; this lane's walk finds a third digest beyond it, so the reproduction is not a restatement of the original observation.

nodes.title: DEF-SCP-01 — EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH conflates supersession with corruption
nodes.statement: The checker hashes working-tree bytes and compares against the recorded digest, so one ERROR code covers two situations demanding opposite responses: an artifact altered behind the ledger's back, and an artifact that legitimately moved on. The deeper finding, which the routing did not state, is that the distinction is not merely uncomputed but uncomputable from what the ledger holds: 0 of 5 hash-bound evidence entries carry any commit the digest was taken at. A lane that shipped only the comparison the defect asks for would produce a checker with nothing to compare against, failing closed across the entire ledger. The mechanism change is therefore a schema addition first and a finding-code split second.
nodes.provenance_basis: DEF-SCP-01. Same class as the five chains already seeded: an alarm that fires on normal operation is a control that will be ignored, which is the estate's own LESSON_DOCUMENTED failure wearing a different hat.

pending_successor.owner: lane D (owning, per DEF-SCP-01 routing); SCP-SI-01 coordinator (declared fallback)
pending_successor.reason: The fix is routed to lane D, which owns failure-to-learning. Lane B's commission is the chain itself. Landing the split from this lane would put two lanes' mechanism changes on one artifact inside one cohort, which is the collision this seed already carries as ICH-03, and would make this lane the producer and the acceptor of its own fix. The chain records the defect with the successor declared, which is what the pending mechanism exists for.
candidate_mechanisms: Add a required recorded_at_commit to every hash-bound ledger evidence entry, and report EVIDENCE_ANCHOR_MISSING where it is absent rather than defaulting to either verdict.
Split the code: EVIDENCE_SUPERSEDED at INFO when the digest was correct at its anchor and has since changed, EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH at ERROR when it was wrong at its own anchor.
Regression test the three cases the defect names, including the one that matters — correct at anchor, changed at tip — asserting INFO and not ERROR.
